newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian coffee auctions to resume on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Indian coffee auctions to resume on Friday.

text.p: India's coffee auctions, suspended since April due to a protest against a turnover tax, will resume on Friday, a senior official at a leading auctioneering firm said.
"Coffee auctions will start tomorrow," Navin Bopaya, a senior official at Karnataka Coffee Brokers Pvt Ltd, told Reuters by telephone from the southern city of Bangalore.
"We have been exempted from the tax." Karnataka Coffee Brokers is one of the four firms which conducts the auction.
Turnover tax is a levy which each dealer and broker has to pay to the state government on coffee sales.
The auctions, by the Indian Coffee Trade Association (ICTA), were suspended on April 1 after the Karnataka government imposed a three percent turnover tax on coffee dealers and brokers.
Bopaya said the government had exempted auctioneers and commission agents from turnover tax. "For others like dealers and packeteers, it has been reduced to one percent," he said.
Last month auctioneers had said that the state government had agreed to their request to waive turnover tax and they were waiting for a formal notification before resuming auctions.
ICTA started conducting auctions in October 1995 after the state-run Coffee Board stopped direct marketing operations.
